question: What should a long term infiltration and inflow strategy do first when a system has many candidate subcatchments?
correctAnswer: Rank subcatchments by how much extraneous flow each one contributes
explanation: Ranking by measured contribution directs early work to the sources that drive wet weather flow, rather than spreading effort evenly.
options: Replace every building lateral in the oldest neighbourhood first
Rank subcatchments by how much extraneous flow each one contributes
Add treatment capacity before measuring where the flow originates
Clean every sewer main twice a year regardless of measured flow
optionA: Replace every building lateral in the oldest neighbourhood first
optionB: Rank subcatchments by how much extraneous flow each one contributes
optionC: Add treatment capacity before measuring where the flow originates
optionD: Clean every sewer main twice a year regardless of measured flow

question: What does climate resilience mean for a wastewater collection system?
correctAnswer: Keeping service working during extreme weather and recovering quickly after it
explanation: Resilience is about maintaining and restoring service under stress, not about eliminating wet weather effects entirely.
options: Removing all storm connections so rainfall no longer affects sewer flows
Building every asset to withstand the largest storm that could be imagined
Keeping service working during extreme weather and recovering quickly after it
Guaranteeing that no overflow can occur under any weather condition at all
optionA: Removing all storm connections so rainfall no longer affects sewer flows
optionB: Building every asset to withstand the largest storm that could be imagined
optionC: Keeping service working during extreme weather and recovering quickly after it
optionD: Guaranteeing that no overflow can occur under any weather condition at all
